plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs like SOXL and SPAL to zero.
Reduce high-beta single names such as METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with conservative limits.
Favor income and broad index exposure for stability.
Maintain a large cash buffer for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5%/month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged and high-beta positions, focusing on lower drawdown.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Reduce exposure to high-beta names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU.
Trim leveraged ETFs SPAL and SOXL to small allocations.
This plan blends broad index and quality tech with reduced leverage.
Maintain a cash buffer of ~10% for risk-first growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall concentration and leverage, aiming for a more stable growth profile with moderate drawdown potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Increase exposure to high-scoring AI/Software names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU.
Add to leveraged ETFs SPAL and SOXL, leaning into higher risk/reward.

Maintain a smaller cash buffer (~5%) for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4%/month by stretching growth and using leverage. It significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell all high-beta single names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU to zero.
Cut all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to near zero.
Increase QQQI exposure to 30% for enhanced income.
Rotate into income/covered-call ETFs for steady monthly distributions.
Prioritize low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan aims for ~1%/month by prioritizing steady distributions and low drawdown. It cuts leverage and high-beta names, focusing on income-generating ETFs. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs, so this is not a savings account.
